findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the ice baffles have an accumulation of soil residues. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and ice machine was immediately removed from service for cleaning. Replacement ice was purchased from an approved source during the inspection. Staff drained, cleaned, and sanitized the ice machine during the inspection and Inspector observed the ice machine to be clean to sight and touch. Ensure ice machine interior is cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following sanitizing operations were operating with too low sanitizer to be effective at sanitizing dishes:
(i) The triple sink was measured at 100 ppm (quaternary ammonium). CORRECTED: Staff determined that an extra pump of sanitizer shall be added to the triple sink to achieve 200ppm (3 pumps total). Inspector observed that the remade solution measured at an effective sanitizer level of 200ppm (quat). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of quaternary ammonium is between 200-400ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
(ii) The chemical dish machine was measured at less than 50ppm (Chlorine). CORRECTED: PIC were informed that the dish machine was too low for sanitizing and removed the dish machine from service immediately; staff instead would only do dishes in the triple sink instead of the supplementary chemical dish machine. Staff contacted a repair person, who arrived during the inspection and adjusted the dish machine. Inspector observes the repaired dish machine is sanitizing at 50ppm (Chlorine). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of Chlorine is between 50-200ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B). [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1ST REPEAT: Observed the following hand sinks to in need of repair:
(i) the hand sink in the hot kitchen appears to be separating from the wall, and there is an accumulation of dust behind it. Ensure this sink is repaired to be sealed to the wall tightly to prevent moisture accumulation between the sink and wall.
(ii) the hand sink in the front bathroom (not under the staircase) is missing sealant between the sink and wall. Silicone sealant will prevent moisture accumulation and microbial growth. 
Inspector and PICs discussed repair options. Ensure both hand sinks are properly sealed to the wall to prevent an accumulation of moisture and soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the cooler at the front service area (by the cash register) was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 50-60F, the internal thermometer was reading at 60F, and the opened jug of milk had an internal temperature of 55F. The PIC voluntary discarded all temperature control for safety (TCS) foods during the inspection: multiple jugs of milk, an opened container of oat milk, and orange juice. Non-TCS foods were kept inside the cooler. The PIC serviced the cooler and noticed a large buildup on the filters. The filters were cleaned but before the inspector left the internal thermometer was observed still at 60F. The cooler may require time for the temperature to come down after cleaning the filters; however, they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is below 41F. They should schedule maintenance if the cooler temperature does not drop below 41F. The inspector will follow-up on 6/24/2025 to check on the temperature of the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed employee using gloved hand to handle cash and credit cards. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that hands are washed after handling possible contaminated items such as cash and credit cards.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine had a concentration of 0 ppm (Cl). The chemical sanitizers for dish machines must have a minimum concentration of 100 ppm. The heat of the dish machine was 111F. The dish machine was tested at the end of the entire cycle and at the end of the rinse cycle. It appears that the dish machine was testing low due to an air bubble in the line. After being properly primed, the dish machine was testing at 100ppm. Owner was initally notified of the concern and could not produce someone knowledgeable about properly using and testing the machine. 
After leaving the facility, the owner called to state the machine was operating properly. CK returned with HM to observe the machine primed at that time with an MJ Kellner representative to service the machine and a chemical log created to monitor the concentration of the machine at least three times per day. Discussed educating staff on service and testing. MJ Kellner representative confirmed he would educate available staff on methods to problem solve.

Ensure that chemical sanitizers meet the proper criteria and are tested regularly.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed in the dry storage area of the production kitchen there is food and single use storage articles (including, but not limited too, sugar, spices, corn syrup, and napkins) being stored on the floor. Ensure that food is stored at least 6-inches off the floor to prevent food from contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the following shelves need to be cleaned: (1) Metal shelves in the walk-in cooler in the production room (REPEAT), and (2) Metal shelves holding bread in the hot kitchen. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
